summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a complex history including kidney transplantation, stage 4 chronic kidney disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, and recent hospitalizations was admitted for acute worsening of dyspnea and orthopnea. Evaluation revealed acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation with bilateral pleural effusions and multifocal pneumonia, likely hospital-acquired. He was treated with intravenous antibiotics, aggressive diuresis, and placement of a right chest tube that drained 2.7 liters of transudative fluid. His respiratory status improved, and he was transitioned to oral diuretics. Tacrolimus was increased due to subtherapeutic levels, and prophylactic vancomycin was used given prior C. difficile history. He stabilized, was weaned off oxygen, and discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up, repeat imaging, and a sleep study due to nocturnal desaturations.
problems: Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Acute kidney failure with tubular necrosis
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Other surgical procedures as the cause of abnormal reaction of the patient, or of later complication, without mention of misadventure at the time of the procedure
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
